Name: Prohibiting the live boiling of crustaceans in food service establishments.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to prohibiting the live boiling of crustaceans in food service establishments

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Health

Summary: This bill would prohibit food service establishments from placing live crustaceans, including, but not limited to, lobsters and crabs, into boiling liquid for cooking. A first violation would carry no monetary penalty with a second or subsequent violation resulting in a civil penalty of up to $100 per violation.
Text:
A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to prohibiting the live boiling of crustaceans in food service establishments

Be it enacted by the Council as follows:


Section 1. Chapter 15 of title 17 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 17-1519 to read as follows:
§ 17-1519 Prohibition on live boiling of crustaceans. a. Definition. For purposes of this section, the term “crustacean” means an aquatic invertebrate belonging to the subphylum Crustacea, including, but not limited to, a lobster or crab intended for human consumption.
b. Prohibition. No food service establishment, or any owner, operator, employee, agent or other person acting on behalf of such establishment, shall place, cause to be placed, or permit the placement of a live crustacean into boiling liquid for the purpose of cooking or preparing such crustacean for human consumption. Nothing in this chapter shall be construed to prohibit any other method used in the cooking or preparation of a crustacean for human consumption.
c. Civil penalty. A food service establishment that violates this chapter or any rule promulgated thereunder shall be subject to a civil penalty of not more than $100; except that there shall be a civil penalty of $0 imposed upon a food service establishment for a first-time violation. The notice of violation for such first-time violation shall inform the food service establishment of the provision of law or rule that the department believes the food service establishment violated, describe the conditions or activity that is the basis for the notice of violation, and advise the food service establishment that the law authorizes civil penalties for such violation and that subsequent violations may result in the imposition of such civil penalties.
§ 2. This local law takes effect 180 days after it becomes law.
